concepts.term: Sound wave travelling through a solid
concepts.def: A sound wave passing into a solid makes the particles of that solid vibrate about their fixed positions. Each particle pushes and pulls its neighbours, so the disturbance is passed on through the material while the material itself stays where it is.
A thin membrane at the inner end of the ear canal. A sound wave arriving through the air makes it vibrate, so it converts a wave disturbance in the air into vibrations of a solid.
Within the ear, sound waves cause the ear drum and other parts to vibrate, and it is these vibrations of solid parts that cause the sensation of sound.

The conversion of sound waves to vibrations of solids works only over a limited frequency range. Outside that range the solid does not respond well enough to the pressure variations for the wave to be converted, however intense the wave is.

Because the conversion of sound waves into vibrations of solids in the ear works only over a limited frequency range, human hearing is itself restricted: the range of normal human hearing is from 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), one hertz being one vibration per second. One kilohertz (kHz) is 1000 Hz, so the upper limit of normal human hearing, 20 kHz, is 20 000 Hz — a thousand times the lower limit of 20 Hz.

concepts.term: Converting between sound waves and vibrations in solids
concepts.def: The conversion works in both directions. A sound wave in air can set a solid vibrating (an ear drum, a microphone diaphragm), and a solid made to vibrate can push on the air and generate a sound wave (a loudspeaker cone, the body of a guitar).

mcqs.q: A hammer strikes one end of a long steel rail. A student with an ear pressed against the far end hears the blow. What is happening inside the steel as the sound travels along it?
options: Particles of the steel vibrate about their positions and pass the disturbance on
Sound slips along the tiny gaps of air trapped between the steel particles
Sound leaves the rail at once and reaches the ear through the air
The rail as a whole slides towards the listener as the wave passes
mcqs.explain: Sound waves can travel through solids causing vibrations in the solid: each particle vibrates and hands the disturbance to its neighbour.

mcqs.q: Music from a loudspeaker in one room can be heard through a solid brick wall in the room next door. Which statement best describes the part the wall plays?
options: It blocks the sound entirely, so what is heard has leaked round the edges
The brick itself vibrates and carries the sound wave to the far side
Sound seeps through the pores of trapped air inside the brick
It reflects the whole wave, so only an echo is heard nearby
mcqs.explain: Sound waves can travel through solids causing vibrations in the solid; the vibrating brick then radiates sound into the second room.

mcqs.q: A sound wave travelling through the air arrives at a person's ear. Which statement describes how this leads to the sensation of sound?
options: The ear drum turns the wave straight into electricity and never moves
The wave passes on unchanged along the ear canal and into the brain
The wave makes the ear drum and other parts of the ear vibrate
The ear amplifies the wave until it is loud enough to hear
mcqs.explain: Within the ear, sound waves cause the ear drum and other parts to vibrate, which causes the sensation of sound.

mcqs.q: A bat call at 45 kHz is played to a class through an ultrasonic transducer at very high intensity. Nobody in the room hears anything. What is the best explanation?
options: The sound is far too quiet by the time that it has reached anybody's ear
A 45 kHz pressure wave in air is not a sound wave, so there is nothing to hear
Only very high frequencies are lost, and hearing them can be trained back
The ear cannot convert a wave of that frequency into vibrations
mcqs.explain: The conversion of sound waves to vibrations of solids works over a limited frequency range, and this restricts the limits of human hearing.

mcqs.q: A singer's voice is picked up by a microphone and played back through a loudspeaker. Which statement correctly describes what happens at the microphone diaphragm and at the loudspeaker cone?
options: Both the diaphragm and the cone turn a sound wave into vibrations of a solid
The diaphragm vibrates the air, while the cone stops the air vibrating
Sound waves set the diaphragm vibrating, and the vibrating cone makes sound waves
Neither part is a solid vibrating, so no conversion of the wave can occur
mcqs.explain: The conversion runs between sound waves and vibrations in solids in both directions, which is exactly what a microphone and a loudspeaker do.

mcqs.q: A drum is struck in a hall and a listener standing a few metres away in the air hears the beat. Which sequence of events describes what happens?
options: Air vibrates first, then the drum skin vibrates, and then the beat is heard
The sound squeezes through tiny air gaps in the floor to get to the listener
The drum skin vibrates and the sound wave itself travels to the brain
The skin vibrates, a sound wave crosses the air, and the ear drum vibrates
mcqs.explain: A vibrating solid generates the sound wave, and the wave then converts back into vibrations of a solid at the ear drum.

mcqs.q: Explain why the process by which the ear detects sound works only over a limited frequency range, and what this means for what a person can hear.
options: Sound waves outside a limited band cannot be converted into vibrations of the ear's solid parts
Outside that band no sound wave exists at all, so there is simply nothing arriving at the ear to detect
The brain selects the frequencies it accepts, so the ear itself passes on every sound wave arriving
The quietest sounds go first, so the range narrows whenever the wave becomes less intense
mcqs.explain: The conversion of sound waves to vibrations of solids works over a limited frequency range, and this restricts the limits of human hearing.

mcqs.q: What is the range of normal human hearing?
options: from 20 Hz to 200 kHz
from 20 Hz to 20 kHz
from 2 Hz to 20 000 Hz
from 20 Hz up to 2000 Hz
mcqs.explain: Students should know that the range of normal human hearing is from 20 Hz to 20 kHz.
